title: Plains Northern Plains Of India
definition: The Northern Plains of India are a vast, fertile aggradational plain formed by the depositional work of three major river systems—the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra—spanning over 3,200 km from west to east.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC CSE Prelims (geomorphological features like Bhabhar, Terai, Bhangar, Khadar) and Mains GS-1 (Physiography, human geography, agricultural sustenance, groundwater depletion, and food security).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Plains Northern Plains Of India.
Evaluate spatial distribution, regional divisions, and depositional landforms.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic Plate Tectonics and Himalayan Orogeny
